newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Saudi Binladen wins $253 mln construction deal.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Binladen wins $253 mln construction deal.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's King Faisal Foundation on Tuesday said it awarded the Saudi Binladen Group a 950 million riyal contract to build what it said would be the biggest complex of its kind in the Middle East.
The complex, know as the Al Faisaliah Centre, will include a hotel, shopping mall, office block and residential accommodation in the Olaya district of central Riyadh.
Binladen beat a host of foreign and local firms to the deal.

Other companies which bid included France's Societe Auxiliaire D'Entreprises in a joint venture with Impregilo SpA of Italy, Dumez International in a joint venture with Britain's Mowlem and Saudi Arabia's El Seif Engineering and Germany's Dykerhoff & Widmann AG in a joint venture with Costain International.

Bids were also received from Joannou & Paraskevaides (Overseas) Ltd of Cyprus in a joint venture with HCB International, Korea's Kukdong Engineering & Construction Co in a joint venture with Shinsung Corp and Saudi Arabia's Consolidated Contractors Co in association with Saudi Arabian Bechtel Co Ltd.
"Construction will start immediately and will be completed early in the year 2000," the foundation said in a statement.
"There has never been a commercial multi-use project of this size in the Middle East," Sean Cuddihy, the foundation's director of engineering and construction, told Reuters.
Cuddihy said an agreement would be signed between Saudi Binladen and the U.S. Turner Steiner Construction Co to provide project management on the 55,000 square metre site.
The centre will boast a 260 metre (850 feet) tower -- the tallest in Saudi Arabia -- providing 30 floors of office space, 100 residential flats and 26,000 square metres of retail space, Cuddihy said.
